from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Convolution starts with a local neighborhood.",
            "Imagine a sliding window over pixels.",
            "This window computes a local weighted average.",
            "It smooths or highlights specific image features.",
            "This process is the discrete convolution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window'", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a 1D sequence
        sequence = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5).add(Integer(i)) for i in range(5)])
        sequence.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(sequence, 'B2', 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(sequence)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        window = Rectangle(width=2.1, height=0.8, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(window, 'B3') # Covering three squares
        self.add(window)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        calc_text = Text("Sum = 1*w1 + 2*w2 + 3*w3", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(calc_text, 'D3')
        self.play(Write(calc_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        result = Integer(6)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(result))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(window.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.7))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Kernel Personalities", ["Different kernels change the image appearance.", "Blur kernels compute local averages.", "Edge detection kernels highlight rapid differences."])
        
        # Create kernel grids
        def create_kernel(values):
            grid = VGroup()
            for row in values:
                for val in row:
                    cell = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=BLUE, stroke_color=WHITE)
                    label = Text(str(val), font_size=20)
                    cell.add(label)
                    grid.add(cell)
            grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0)
            return grid

        # Kernel configurations
        k_identity = create_kernel([[0,0,0], [0,1,0], [0,0,0]])
        k_blur = create_kernel([[1/9, 1/9, 1/9], [1/9, 1/9, 1/9], [1/9, 1/9, 1/9]])
        k_edge = create_kernel([[-1,-1,-1], [-1,8,-1], [-1,-1,-1]])

        # Place them
        self.place_at_grid(k_identity, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(k_blur, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(k_edge, 'B2')
        k_blur.set_opacity(0)
        k_edge.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(k_identity))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(k_identity, k_blur))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(k_blur, k_edge))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "CNNs treat kernels as learnable parameters.",
            "Layers learn filters for specific shapes.",
            "AI uses these to detect complex objects."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("CNNs: Learning Kernels", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visuals: Input image representation
        img_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, color=GRAY) for _ in range(16)]).arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(img_grid, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(img_grid), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visuals: Filter sliding
        filter_box = Square(side_length=1.4, color=BLUE).set_stroke(width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_box, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(filter_box))
        
        target_pos = self.grid["B3"]
        self.play(filter_box.animate.move_to(target_pos), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visuals: Resulting Feature Map
        feature_map = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=GREEN) for _ in range(4)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 2, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(feature_map, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(feature_map), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept (1 minute)
sections.content: Introduce the idea of a 'local average.' Use the analogy of a fuzzy camera lens: how each pixel's color is influenced by its neighbors. Explain that convolution is a systematic way to slide a small grid (the kernel) over a larger grid (the image) to compute new values.
sections.example: A 3x3 grid sliding over a 5x5 pixel array, showing the center pixel being recalculated as the weighted average of its 8 neighbors.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mechanism (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Define discrete convolution as the element-wise multiplication of the kernel and the image patch, followed by a summation. Emphasize the 'Flip and Slide' rule—visualize the kernel reflecting before sliding, ensuring the mathematical definition aligns with spatial filtering.
sections.example: A 2x2 kernel sliding over a matrix of numbers; display a simple animation showing 'Multiply and Sum' happening in real-time as the kernel moves.

sections.title: Kernel Personalities: Shaping Data (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Explain how different kernels produce different outcomes. A 'Blur' kernel averages neighbors; an 'Edge Detection' kernel calculates differences between neighbors. This is the foundation of how computers 'see' shapes.
sections.example: A cute character icon: Show the 'Blur' kernel making it fuzzy, then a 'Sobel' kernel drawing only the outline of the character.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Convolutional Neural Networks (1 minute)
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the math to AI. Explain that CNNs don't just use fixed kernels—the network 'learns' the best kernel values to detect eyes, ears, or whiskers in images.
sections.example: An animation of a computer looking at a photograph of a cat; different kernels highlighting the cat's whiskers versus its ears as the layers of the network process the image.
